newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission to decide new rice import proposal.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to decide new rice import proposal.

text.p: The European Commission won the right to decide on a new rice import system on Tuesday after a trade committee failed to achieve a majority vote, a Commission official said.

Because a vote was taken at the European Union's specially convened rice management committee, the final decision now rests with the Commission to implement the new, cumulative rice tariff recovery system.
"The responsibility now rests with the Commission which will decide what to do in the light of other factors," the official said.
The decision to introduce the new system led to a dispute 18 months ago with the United States which has launched a complaint at the World Trade Organisation in Geneva.
The dispute arose because of a 63,000-tonne tariff-free quota under the GATT world trade agreement.
The United States won a specific quota to export 8,000 tonnes of brown rice and 36,000 tonnes of partly processed rice to the EU.
But the EU decided that the original tariff system based on invoices was open to fraud and proposed a system based on market reference prices.
The U.S. complained that its traders were losing money and was offered a cumulative recovery system .
The new proposal ran into trouble when EU member states failed to agree in the management committee following strong opposition from European rice millers.
The issue is now linked to a proposal for a 30,000-tonne annual quota for the import of malting barley from the United States.
This is also the subject of a WTO complaint by the U.S. and is due to be discussed by farm ministers late on Tuesday.
Some member states have complained that the proposal would affect only one American brewing operation in Europe.
Both proposals have now been made conditional on the withdrawal by the U.S. of the WTO complaints, an EU member state official said on Tuesday. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
